landing.heroDescription: Clann is a private family tree app. Record people, build relationships, and explore your ancestry through an interactive visual graph — all stored on your own server.
landing.ctaText: Ready to start mapping your family?

tree.title: Interactive Family Tree
tree.description: Visualise up to two generations of ancestors, plus children and spouses, in a colour-coded graph. Toggle between vertical and horizontal layouts, pan, zoom, and click any node to navigate.

relationships.title: Relationships
relationships.description: Link people as Father, Mother, Sibling, or Spouse. Adding a sibling automatically inherits the parent's parents. Spouse relationships carry optional from/to dates.

photos.title: Photos
photos.description: Upload a JPEG or PNG photo (up to 3 MB) for each person. Photos appear on profile cards, detail pages, and directly in the family tree graph.

export.title: Export
export.description: Download the family tree as a JPEG image to share with family, or as a structured JSON file for archiving or importing into other tools.

login.termsContent:
Last updated: March 2026

**1. Acceptance of Terms**
By creating an account and using Clann, you agree to be bound by these Terms & Conditions. If you do not agree, please do not register.

**2. Use of the Service**
Clann is a private family tree application. You may use it solely for personal, non-commercial purposes — recording and exploring your own family history. You must not use the service for any unlawful purpose or in any way that could harm others.

**3. Your Account**
You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your login credentials and for all activity that occurs under your account. Please choose a strong password and keep it secure.

**4. Your Data**
All family data you enter — people, relationships, photos, and biographies — is stored on the server you connect to. You are responsible for the accuracy of the data you enter. Do not upload content that infringes third-party rights or that you do not have permission to share.

**5. Privacy**
Clann does not share your personal data with third parties. Your data is used solely to provide the service. The application stores a session token in your browser's local storage to keep you logged in.

**6. Termination**
You may delete your account at any time. We reserve the right to suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms.

**7. Disclaimer**
The service is provided 'as is' without warranties of any kind. We are not liable for any loss or damage arising from your use of the service.

**8. Changes to These Terms**
We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the service after changes constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.

**9. Application Disclaimer**
By creating an account, you confirm that you have read and are familiar with the Disclaimer, which sets out the conditions of use of the basic Clann service. The Disclaimer is accessible at any time from the footer of the application.

help.title: Help & Documentation
help.subtitle: Learn how to use Clann to build and explore your family tree.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.step1Body: Click Sign In and choose Create Account. Enter a username, first name, surname, sex, email address, and password (at least 8 characters). You will receive a confirmation email — click the link to activate your account.
gettingStarted.step2Body: On your first login, Clann automatically creates a family tree named after your surname and adds you as the first family member using the details you provided at registration. You can find your tree in the navigation bar dropdown and edit your entry at any time.
gettingStarted.step3Body: Your own entry is already in the tree. Click Add Person in the navigation bar to add other family members. Fill in the first name, family name, and sex (required). Optionally add birth and death dates and places, a biography, and a photo.
gettingStarted.step4Body: Open a person's profile and go to the Relationships tab. Click + Add Relationship to link them as Father, Mother, Sibling, or Spouse of another person in your tree.

people.title: Managing People
people.fieldsBody: Each person has: First Name and Family Name (required), Middle Name, Sex (required), Date and Place of Birth, Date and Place of Death, Nickname, Username, Email, Identity Verified flag, and a Biography (supports markdown — rendered in the Life Story tab).
people.photoBody: On a person's detail page, click the avatar to open the photo uploader. Drag and drop a JPEG or PNG file (up to 3 MB), or click to browse. Photos appear on cards, detail pages, and in the family tree graph.
people.editBody: Open a person's profile and click Edit to update their details. To delete, click Delete on the profile page or the trash icon on a family member card. Deletion cannot be undone.

relationships.title: Relationships
relationships.typesBody: You can link people as Father, Mother, Sibling (Brother or Sister), or Spouse. Open a person's profile, go to the Relationships tab, and click + Add Relationship to choose the type and the related person.
relationships.siblingBody: When you add siblings you can select multiple people at once — hold the list open and tap each name. Clann automatically assigns the same Father and Mother to every new sibling, so you only need to record parents once.
relationships.parentTitle: Setting a parent builds your tree automatically
relationships.parentBody: When you set a Father or Mother for a person, Clann looks up that parent's other children and automatically links them as siblings. This is a powerful way to build a comprehensive family tree quickly — add a shared parent once and the sibling network fills in for you.
relationships.filterBody: The person picker filters by sex to show only relevant matches: Father shows males, Mother shows females, Brother shows males, and Sister shows females. This makes it faster to find the right person in large families.
relationships.spouseBody: Spouse relationships can carry optional From and To dates (free-form text, e.g. "1990" or "2 June 2001"). Set them when adding the relationship, or edit them inline in the Relationships tab.

familyTree.title: Family Tree
familyTree.overviewBody: The tree shows the selected person (root) at the centre, up to two generations of ancestors above, direct children below, and spouses to the side. Click any person's name in the family list to open their tree.
familyTree.coloursBody: Emerald = you (root) · Blue = Father side · Rose = Mother side · Amber = Children · Violet = Spouse · Teal = Sibling. The legend is shown at the bottom of the tree.
familyTree.navigationBody: Pan by clicking and dragging. Zoom with the scroll wheel or pinch gesture. Click any node to open that person's profile. Hover over a node to see a tooltip with date of birth, place of birth, and biography.
familyTree.orientationBody: Use the Vertical / Horizontal buttons in the tree toolbar to toggle the layout. Vertical places ancestors above and children below. Horizontal places ancestors to the right and children to the left.
familyTree.exportBody: Click the Export button in the toolbar to choose a format: JPEG downloads a snapshot image of the visible tree, JSON downloads all people and relationships in Clann's own format, and GEDCOM downloads a .ged file compatible with other genealogy apps such as Ancestry, FamilySearch, and Gramps.
familyTree.mediaLibraryBody: If your account includes access to the Ullav Digital Asset Management system, a Media Library button appears in the tree toolbar. Clicking it opens the DAM browser in a new tab and signs you in automatically — no second login needed.

familyList.title: Family Members List
familyList.viewsBody: Switch between a responsive card grid and a sortable table using the Cards / List toggle at the top of the Family Members page. The card view shows photos; the list view is better for sorting.
familyList.searchBody: Type in the search box to filter by name instantly. In list view, click any column header (Family Name, Date of Birth, Place of Birth) to sort. Empty values always sort to the bottom.
familyList.paginationBody: Use the Per page selector (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, or 30) to control how many people appear at once. Navigate with the numbered page buttons or Prev / Next. The page resets to 1 whenever you search or change the page size.

lifeStory.title: Life Story
lifeStory.overviewTitle: What is the Life Story panel?
lifeStory.overviewBody: Every person has a Life Story tab on their profile page. It renders the biography field as formatted text — headings, paragraphs, bold, italics, lists, and links are all supported.
lifeStory.editingBody: Open a person's profile and click Edit. The Biography field has a built-in markdown editor with a toolbar. Write freely and use the toolbar buttons for formatting. Click Save Changes when done.
lifeStory.markdownBody: The editor uses Markdown: # Heading 1, ## Heading 2, **bold**, *italic*, - bullet list, 1. numbered list, [link text](url). The Life Story tab renders the final result.
lifeStory.lifeImageBody: A larger portrait or scene image can be added to the Life Story tab. Open a person's profile, go to the Life Story tab, and click '+ Add Life Story Image' (or hover over the existing image and click Change). Drag and drop a JPEG or PNG (up to 2 MB) into the upload area. The image appears at the top left of the Life Story panel with the biography flowing to its right.
lifeStory.exportPdfBody: Click the 'Export as PDF' button at the top of the Life Story tab to open your browser's print dialog. Choose 'Save as PDF' (or the equivalent in your browser) to download a formatted PDF. The file is named after the person. The PDF includes their name, birth details, life story image, and full biography.
lifeStory.mediaLibraryTitle: Inserting images from the media library
lifeStory.mediaLibraryBody: While editing a biography, click 'Browse media library' below the editor to open an inline media picker. Click any image to insert it at your current cursor position, or drag it from the picker onto the drop zone below the editor. Images are inserted as thumbnails. A green confirmation message appears briefly to confirm the insertion.

lifeEvents.title: Life Events
lifeEvents.overviewBody: Each person has a Life Events tab on their profile page. It shows a chronological timeline of significant moments — birth, marriage, graduation, immigration, military service, and more. Events are sorted by date; undated events appear at the end.
lifeEvents.timelineBody: Events appear as cards on a left-spine timeline, each with a coloured icon badge that reflects the event type. The icon and colour are chosen automatically: emerald for Birth, violet for Marriage, blue for Graduation, red for Military service, sky for Immigration and Emigration, amber for Divorce, stone for Death, and grey for Other or custom types.
lifeEvents.addingBody: On the Life Events tab, click 'Add Event'. Enter the event name, an optional date (free-form text is accepted: '1920', 'circa 1920', 'June 1920'), and choose an event type. Select 'Custom type…' to enter your own label. Click Save when done.
lifeEvents.viewingBody: Events that have a story, source link, or source assets show a 'Details' pill in the top-right corner of their card. Click it to expand an inline panel showing the full story rendered as formatted text, a clickable external source link, and links to any source image or document. Click 'Close' to collapse the panel.
lifeEvents.editingBody: Hover over any event card and click the pencil icon to open the inline edit panel. Update the name, date, type, and short description, or write a longer narrative in the Story field (markdown is supported, with media library image insertion). Click 'Save Changes' to apply. The delete button removes the event permanently. Edit and delete are only available to the person's owner and admins.
lifeEvents.sourcesBody: Each event can have an external source URL, a source image, and a source document — all linked from your media library. Tick the Verified checkbox once you have confirmed the event against a reliable source. These fields help document the evidence behind your family history.

research.title: Research
research.overviewBody: The Research page gives you a dedicated workspace for capturing and organising the information you gather while researching your family tree. It is linked to the active family tree and accessible from the main navigation bar.
research.notesBody: Each note has a title, an optional one-line description, and a body written in markdown — the same rich text format used in biographies and life event stories. Notes are listed on the left; selecting one opens it in the reading panel on the right. Click 'New Note' to create one.
research.editingBody: Click the pencil icon on any note card, or click 'Edit' in the reading panel, to open the editor. The body field supports full markdown with a live preview. If you have media library access, use the 'Browse media library' link above the editor to pick an image — it is inserted at the cursor position as an inline markdown image.
research.foldersBody: Create folders to organise your research notes by topic. Click the + button next to the Folders heading in the sidebar to create a new folder. In the reading panel, use the 📁 folder dropdown to move the current note into any folder. The Unfiled Notes view shows all notes that have not been assigned to a folder. Click the ↻ button in the folder header to refresh the note list without reloading the page.
research.sharingBody: When your active tree is linked to a team, a share toggle appears in the note editor. Switch it on (👥 Shared with team) to make the note visible to all active team members; switch it off (🔒 Private) to keep it visible only to you. A badge on each note card and in the reading panel shows the privacy status. Team trees also show a 'Shared by team' folder in the sidebar — selecting it shows notes shared by other team members at a glance.
research.repliesBody: Shared notes have a Replies section at the bottom of the reading panel. Any team member can post a reply: type in the box and click Post reply. Each reply shows the author's name with a coloured initial badge — emerald for your own replies, violet for others'. The total number of replies appears as a 💬 badge on the note card in the sidebar.
research.wikiBody: Click the '🌐 Wikipedia' button in the header to open an inline Wikipedia search panel. Type a name, place, or event to see results. Select a result to read the article summary. Click 'Save as Note' to create a new research note pre-filled with the article title and extract, including a citation link back to Wikipedia. The search uses the Wikipedia edition matching your current language setting.
research.censusBody: Click the '📜 1926 Census' button to open the census panel. Enter a surname, first name, and county to pre-fill your search, then click the search button to open the National Archives of Ireland website in a new tab with your terms already entered. The panel shows what the census records contain — name, age, occupation, religion, birthplace, Irish language ability, household members, and location.
research.censusAttributionBody: The 1926 Census records are published by the National Archives of Ireland under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0). Records may be freely used with attribution. The census is being released in phases — not all counties or households may be available yet.

aiAssistant.title: AI Research Assistant
aiAssistant.overviewTitle: What is the AI Research Assistant?
aiAssistant.overviewBody: The AI Research Assistant is a genealogy-focused chat panel on the Research page. It connects to your choice of AI provider using your own API key, so your data stays under your control. Use it to research any family tree — your own ancestry, a historical family, a royal lineage, or any other genealogical subject. Ask for help with record lookups, historical context, name research, DNA analysis, and research strategy.
aiAssistant.setupBody: Go to Settings (your username in the navigation bar → Settings). Choose a provider, select a model, and paste your API key. The key is encrypted before being stored — Clann never keeps it in plain text. For Ollama (the local, free option), enter the URL of your running Ollama server instead of an API key.
aiAssistant.providersBody: Anthropic (Claude Sonnet, Haiku, Opus), OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini), and Ollama (any locally running model, defaulting to llama3.2). Anthropic Claude gives the best reasoning for complex genealogy questions. OpenAI GPT-4o is broadly capable and widely familiar. Ollama runs entirely on your own machine — no API key needed and no data leaves your computer.
aiAssistant.startingBody: Open the Research page from the navigation bar and click the '🤖 AI Assistant' button in the header. The chat panel opens on the right. Type your question and press Send or hit Enter. Responses stream in real time. Click 'Clear' in the chat header to start a fresh conversation.
aiAssistant.templatesBody: Click '📋 Prompt templates' below the input field to open a panel of ready-made genealogy prompts organised into six categories: Records & Archives, Names & Origins, Emigration, Research Strategy, Historical Context, and DNA. Click any template to fill the input — you can edit it before sending. When researching a specific person, additional person-specific prompts appear at the top of the panel.
aiAssistant.personContextBody: Open any person's profile and go to the Relationships, Life Story, or Life Events tab. Click 'Research with AI' to open the chat pre-loaded with that person's details — name, dates, places, biography, and known relationships. Their name appears as a badge above the chat and the input placeholder prompts you to ask about them directly.
aiAssistant.treeContextTitle: Including your family tree as context
aiAssistant.treeContextBody: Click the '🌳 Include tree' badge above the chat to inject everyone in your active family tree into the AI's context. This lets the AI reason about relationships, spot patterns across generations, and make suggestions tailored to your tree. A count badge shows how many people were loaded. Click again to remove the tree context.
aiAssistant.saveBody: Each AI response has a '📋 Save as Note' button at the bottom of the message. Clicking it creates a new Research Note pre-filled with the AI's response, ready to edit and save. To save the entire conversation, click 'Save Conversation' in the chat header — it creates a single note containing the full thread formatted as a dialogue.
aiAssistant.historyBody: Every conversation is automatically saved and linked to your active family tree. Click '🕐 History' in the chat header to see all past sessions, each named after its opening question. Click any session to restore the full conversation and continue exactly where you left off. This is useful when a research thread spans multiple sittings — find a new document, come back, and pick up the thread without re-typing any context. Delete sessions you no longer need using the ✕ button on hover.
aiAssistant.digDeeperTitle: Dig deeper with AI from a note
aiAssistant.digDeeperBody: When you are viewing a research note, click the '🤖 Dig deeper with AI' button in the note header. This opens the AI chat with the note's title and content injected automatically as context — an amber badge confirms which note is loaded. This bridges your written research and the AI: instead of copy-pasting context manually, the AI picks up from exactly what you have already documented. Use it when you hit a dead end in a note and want AI help on the specific gap you identified. The note context is cleared when you close the AI panel.

multipleTrees.title: Multiple Family Trees
multipleTrees.manageBody: Use the tree selector in the navigation bar to create new trees and switch between them. The currently selected tree is shown in the nav bar. Selecting a different tree takes you straight to that tree's family members page.
multipleTrees.primaryBody: One tree per account is marked as primary (shown with a gold badge in the dropdown). Promote any other tree to primary using the star icon. The primary tree cannot be deleted — promote another tree first if you need to remove it.
multipleTrees.exportBody: Open any person's profile, go to the Family Tree tab, and click the Export button in the toolbar to choose a format — JPEG, JSON, or GEDCOM.
multipleTrees.importBody: Click the tree selector in the nav bar and choose 'Import tree…'. Upload a Clann JSON export or a GEDCOM (.ged) file. You will see a preview of the people and relationships found. Give the new tree a name and click Start import.

teams.title: Teams
teams.whatBody: Teams let you share a family tree with other Clann users in read-only mode. A team has an owner (the person who created it), an optional purpose description, and a list of members. Members can view any tree the owner has linked to the team — they cannot add, edit, or delete people or relationships. Teams are available to Family, Professional, and Enterprise subscribers.
teams.createBody: If you hold a Family, Professional, or Enterprise subscription, you can create a team from the Team page, accessible via the navigation bar. Give your team a name and an optional description of its purpose. Only one team per account is supported.
teams.inviteBody: From the Team page, click 'Invite member' and enter the email address of the person you want to invite. They will receive an email with a link to accept or decline the invitation. Invited members must have a Clann account, or they can create one when they follow the invitation link.
teams.acceptBody: When you receive a team invitation by email, click the link in the message. If you are already signed in to Clann, you will be shown the team name and owner and can choose to accept or decline. If you are not signed in, you will be redirected to log in first and then taken back to the invitation. Accepted members appear in the team's Members list.
teams.linkTreeTitle: Linking a tree to your team
teams.linkTreeBody: As the team owner, go to the Team page and select the 'Linked Trees' tab. Click 'Link a tree' to choose one of your family trees to share with team members. A tree can be linked to one team at a time. To unlink it, select it from the list and choose 'Unlink'.
teams.sharedTreeBody: When a tree has been shared with you through a team, it appears in the 'Shared with me' section of the tree selector in the navigation bar. Selecting it switches the active tree to the shared one. A violet banner at the top of the page confirms you are in read-only view — you can browse all family members and the family tree graph, but adding or editing is not available.
teams.manageBody: The Team page shows tabs for Members, Linked Trees, and Purpose. As the owner, you can edit the team name and purpose, invite and remove members, and link or unlink trees. The Danger Zone at the bottom of the page lets you delete the team — this removes all members and unlinks all trees, but does not delete any family trees or their data.

gedcom.title: GEDCOM Exchange
gedcom.whatBody: GEDCOM (Genealogical Data Communication) is the standard file format used by genealogy applications worldwide — including Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps, MacFamilyTree, and many others. Clann supports GEDCOM 5.5.1 for both export and import, letting you move data between tools freely.
gedcom.exportBody: Open any person's profile, go to the Family Tree tab, and click the Export button, then choose 'Export as GEDCOM'. Clann fetches all people and relationships in the active tree, converts them to GEDCOM format, and downloads a .ged file named after the tree. You can then open this file in any genealogy application.
gedcom.importBody: Click the tree selector in the nav bar and choose 'Import tree…'. Drop or browse to your .ged file. Clann reads all INDI (person) and FAM (family) records, derives parent, spouse, and sibling relationships automatically, and shows a preview before importing. The imported data becomes a new tree — your existing trees are untouched.
gedcom.warningsBody: If Clann cannot fully resolve a record — for example a person with no SEX field, or a FAM that references an unknown individual — it makes a best-fit decision (defaulting sex to Male, skipping the unresolvable link) and lists the issue in an amber warnings panel before you confirm the import. Review the list and fix anything that needs attention after the import completes.
gedcom.includedBody: Exported: name (given, middle, surname, nickname), sex, birth and death dates and places, biography (as a GEDCOM NOTE), and all parent/spouse/sibling relationships including marriage dates. Not exported: profile photos, life story images, username, email, or identity-verified flag — these are Clann-specific fields with no GEDCOM equivalent.
gedcom.compatBody: Clann writes GEDCOM 5.5.1 with UTF-8 encoding and CRLF line endings, which is accepted by all major genealogy apps. Date fields are stored as free-form text in Clann, so they are passed through as-is; standard GEDCOM date formats (e.g. '12 JUN 1950') will be interpreted correctly by other apps, while informal formats (e.g. 'around 1950') may appear as notes. When importing from other apps, ANSEL-encoded files may have character encoding issues — re-saving as UTF-8 in the source app first resolves this.

contactUs.title: Contact Us
contactUs.supportBody: For technical issues, account questions, or anything not working as expected, email us at support@ullav.com. Please include steps to reproduce the problem, what you expected to happen, what actually happened, and any screenshots that help explain the issue.
contactUs.contactBody: For general questions, partnerships, or press enquiries, get in touch at info@ullav.com.
contactUs.accountBody: To request deletion of your account and all associated data, or to suggest a new feature, email support@ullav.com. Please include your username in account-related requests.

disclaimer.content:
The basic Clann solution can be used free of charge under the conditions outlined here.
If you do not wish to adhere to these conditions, you should delete your account.

1. If you add information to the Clann database, you are responsible for the accuracy of that data.
2. You should regularly back up your data using the export function in the application. You are fully responsible if your data is lost or becomes unavailable.
3. Note that images uploaded in the basic application are not exported, so you should maintain your own copies of these images if you wish to use them outside of the application.
4. The data you store in the Clann database is never (and never will be) made available to third parties under any circumstances.
5. The Clann app uses automated translation for text, which are not guaranteed to be 100% accurate. In all cases, the English text is the primary language to be used in any discussions about the scope and use of the application.
